stem: In the formula $I=\dfrac{1}{2}M\left(a^2+b^2\right)$, $a={=a}$, $M={=M}$ and $I={=I}$. Mark on the number line every value of $b$ that makes the formula true.
solution: Put the three given numbers into $I=\dfrac{1}{2}M\left(a^2+b^2\right)$, so that $b$ is the only letter left.
Undo what multiplies the bracket by doing the same to both sides: multiply by 2, then divide by $M$.
Subtract the number $a^2$ from both sides so that $b^2$ stands alone and equals a positive number.
Take the square root of both sides: the positive root and its negative both square to this number, so $b$ has two values.
Tap both values on the number line, one on each side of 0.
notes: Standard tier because the square root comes after three undoing steps and a subtraction, not one. Row 1 is the anchor's own numbers (a=4, M=8, I=320, b=±8); every row checked: ½M(a²+b²) = I with whole-number roots inside the ±10 range. Same single diagnostic and same limits as the basic template: the symbolic half of the objective is a gap; extra-values and sign-flipped are deliberately not mapped; missed-values also fires when only the negative root was marked, so feedback must not presume which root is missing.
